From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — TCO follow-up and next tests

Hi Sam — great to meet you and Olivia today. Per our call, summary + next steps below.

Summary (short):
- FinPay goal: move high-volume inference for transaction enrichment and customer messaging to a cost-predictable, low-latency runtime.
- Hyperscaler comparison: SageMaker/Vertex have broader infra but tend to be more expensive per-token at our batch and cache assumptions; they do offer integrated infra + infra credits which matter for large commitments.

Requested deliverables from Redwood (attached):
- Per-1M token cost model (base): see attached RW_TCO_Estimate_FinPay_v2.xlsx
- Performance report samples: redwood-perf-metrics.pdf (latency & throughput profiles)
- Canary test plan: redwood-canary-test-plan.md (short-lived, 7-day run)

High-level per-1M token numbers (ballpark; will finalize after workload sampling):
- Hosted Redwood (standard): $28–$35 / 1M tokens (depends on model family and quantization)
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, amortized): $18–$24 / 1M tokens (with 3–6 month commit)
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints (SageMaker/Vertex): $35–$50 / 1M tokens (including infra egress and provisioning overhead)

Assumptions behind numbers (short):
- Tokenization & model mix: 70% assistant-style completions (context + generation), 30% embeddings/rerank.
- Batching: typical batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU cost by ~15–30% depending on QPS patterns; our numbers assume 1.6x effective batching for average workload.
- Cache hit rate: we model two scenarios: 10% (low), 40% (moderate). Each +10% cache hit reduces billed generation tokens proportionally and reduces latency.
- KV cache reuse for conversational flows reduces decoding token cost substantially for chat-like sessions.

Proposed next tests (we can run within 48–72 hours once we have routing keys and a sample prompt set):
1) 7-day canary (50k–100k tokens/day): measure p50/p95 latency, per-1M cost, and achieved batching/caching rates.
2) Cost sensitivity: run two configs — (A) hosted/default batching, (B) dedicated-like instance with aggressive batching & quantized model — compare unit economics.
3) Regression checks: run a small eval prompt set (~200 cases) to verify output quality vs your current baseline.

Attachments: RW_TCO_Estimate_FinPay_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with line-items), redwood-perf-metrics.pdf.

Next steps:
- Olivia: send sample prompt set + preferred time window for the canary (we recommend low-traffic window to start).
- Aditya/Marcus: we will set up test infra and share a short runbook.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min alignment call if helpful.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Olivia — small add from our ops side on test design. Proposed canary plan (excerpt):

- Duration: 7 days (72 hours warmup + 5 days steady)
- Traffic split: route 2% of production traffic (~50k tokens/day) to Redwood hosted for config A; route another 2% to dedicated-like config B (same prompt set).
- Metrics to capture: token counts (input vs generated), cache-hit rate, batch sizes, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, effective cost per 1M tokens (including infra).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 450ms, cost delta vs baseline <= 15% (for config B we expect lower cost).

We'll provision test endpoints and share a DocuSign test access agreement (minimal) — link: https://hubspot.example/deal/2345/documents/test-access.

I've attached a short canary runbook (redwood-canary-test-plan.md) and a preliminary TCO calc (RW_TCO_Estimate_FinPay_v2.xlsx). Marcus will monitor the run and provide daily standups in the shared channel.

—Marcus
